title: Iran sees threats, opportunities but little deterrence in Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan pact, says Hamidreza Azizi
gist: A mutual defense pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, signed amid the Iran war, aims to shore up Saudi security and deter Houthi attacks, but analysis suggests it offers Riyadh little real deterrence while creating both threats and openings for Tehran.

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a mutual defense pact against the backdrop of the Iran war, a conflict that has hurt Gulf countries, especially Saudi Arabia, more than any others.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A formalized Gulf-Turkey-Pakistan security bloc changes the regional alliance map and could shape future defense procurement and basing decisions.
insights.locator: The mutual defense pact signed between the regional Muslim powers

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia's oil sales have plummeted and its energy infrastructure has been badly damaged as a result of the Iran war.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Damaged Saudi energy infrastructure and reduced oil sales are a direct supply-side risk factor for oil markets and Saudi fiscal revenue.
insights.quote: Saudi Arabia's oil sales have plummeted. Its energy infrastructure is badly damaged.
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia's oil sales have plummeted

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia hopes the defense pact with Turkey and Pakistan will help deter further attacks on it from Iran-backed Houthi forces.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: If the pact fails to deter Houthi attacks, Saudi energy and shipping infrastructure remains exposed despite the new alliance.
insights.locator: It hopes Turkey and Pakistan's help will deter

insights.claim: Iran scholar Hamidreza Azizi assesses that Tehran sees both threats and opportunities in the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan pact but views it as providing little actual deterrence against Iran.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A pact widely framed as anti-Iran deterrence may be discounted by Tehran, meaning it may not change Iran's calculus toward Gulf targets or shipping.
insights.locator: Iran scholar Hamidreza Azizi discusses what the pact means
